notes.title: Dev Progress + Release Date News
notes.content:
Development Progress
It’s been radio silence for a few months regarding any news about the game, but I’m here to assure you that development is still going strong! Aside from a few occasional pauses due to personal health reasons, I’ve been working hard to get this game to completion. Here’s what I’ve been working on over the past few months:

Controller mapping: This was relatively simple considering the game has minimal controls, though I still need to make the UI controller-friendly.

Chapter 2 level design: Things really start to escalate here; The atmosphere becomes much more unsettling and mysterious.

Chapter 2 storyline: More eventful story beats unfold, uncovering the grim reality of what happened to the family in the house Emma is trapped in.

Chapter 3 level design: Without spoiling too much, let’s just say this chapter will tie up many loose threads and take place in an entirely different environment.

Minor quality-of-life changes: Improved FOV, subtle highlights on objects Emma reacts to, and minor lighting tweaks.

On top of this, I’ve been tinkering with FL Studio and learning to make simple music tracks! It’s mostly experimental, but there’s a good chance I’ll compose something ambient for the game.
Release Date
To be honest, it’s been difficult to pin down an estimated release date. Initially, I was confident the game would be done by the end of August, but I couldn’t have been more wrong. Every internal deadline I’ve set for myself has ended up taking longer than expected, so I don’t want to give a date only to postpone it again.

That being said, I’m working on a trailer that I plan to upload once the game’s development is 99% complete. This will serve as the release announcement trailer, and by that point, I’ll be confident there won’t be any further delays.

Thank you for your patience! If you’d like to keep up with my day-to-day updates, I frequently post on X and Instagram:

X - https://x.com/dev_mustang
Instagram - https://www.instagram.com/mustang_dev

notes.title: INDIE GAME UTSAV SALE + Demo Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 
I am happy to announce that Blinding Oversight is now part of the Indie Game Utsav event! This event showcases amazing games made by Indian developers and you should definitely check them out. Big thanks to Nodwin Gaming and Nodding Heads Games for hosting the event on Steam!

Check out the sale page here: https://store.steampowered.com/sale/ComicConxIndieGameUtsav

Before I begin listing the changes I have made, I want to give a huge thanks to everyone who has played the demo and wishlisted the game so far! Progress has been steady, and soon I will be updating the art capsule and logo as well. Now let's list the changes!

 Added a "Photo-sensitivity Warning" screen at the start of the game. My apologies for not adding this warning earlier.
 Added a small tip that shows what the controls are. This should have also been added earlier, I cannot expect everyone to assume "E" is the interact button. Whoops!
 Lighting has been improved in certain areas of the map.
 Audio has been fixed so they're not loud but also directional.

notes.title: Minor Demo Update
notes.content:
Hey everyone, I've done a few minor changes to the User Interface of the demo:

 The resolution selection is now a dropdown list instead of a horizontal selector.
 Added a brightness bar to change the gamma of the game. The difference will be pretty minor. A very bright scene would not match with the intended atmosphere of the game.


If you wish to talk to the developer of the game, feel free to join the discord: https://discord.gg/huCjEr7

notes.title: Updates to the Demo
notes.content:
Hello everyone, thank you for taking your time to try the demo! I had to rush some of the work to have the demo ready for the next fest, but I will continue to push updates that will make the gameplay a little smoother and cleaner.

Here are some changes I have added since the first release of the demo:

 Minor bug fixes that made objects disappear when they shouldn't
 Fixed stutters that were caused during specific key events
 Some UI elements did not work like they were intended to


And now I will list some of the updates you can expect in the coming days! These were thanks to the feedback everyone has provided so far.


 Brightness/Gamma setting that can help some players to see the house a little better.
 More object interactions that help connect pieces of the story
 Better UI elements (The resolution dropdown has been a pain to deal with but we're getting there)
 Smoother UI experience (fading, more intuitive sounds)
 Displaying input controls at the beginning of the game
 Controller support!
 Minor bug fixes


This section will be the beginning of the final game, so any improvements on the demo will directly benefit the full release. But that being said, this chapter will have more content in the final release of the game that the demo may not have. Possibly more events, paintings and objects to interact with!
